newsitem.title: IRAQ: 1,000 Iraqi pilgrims set out for Mecca.
newsitem.headline: 1,000 Iraqi pilgrims set out for Mecca.

text.p: Some 1,000 Iraqi Moslems left for Saudi Arabia on Monday for the haj, the first group from Iraq to perform the annual pilgrimage to Mecca since 1994, officials said.

Officials at the Endowment and Religious Affairs Ministry said the pilgrims, accompanied by a medical team, left in a convoy of 25 buses on the 24-hour journey. They will have to go through immigration at the Saudi border post of Ar'ar.

Iraq stopped sending pilgrims to the haj in 1995, saying U.N. trade sanctions imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait had emptied its coffers of hard cash. Some 500 Iraqis travelled by land to Saudi Arabia for the 1994 haj.
Iraq, with a population of 20 million, can send up to 20,000 pilgrims to Mecca under quotas set by the Organisation of the Islamic Conference.
But officials said financial constraints forced the authorities to limit the number to about 1,000 this year. Every pilgrim is allowed to carry $500 with him.

Pleas by Iraq to have part of its assets frozen abroad released for haj purposes have gone unheeded. The United Nations also rejected a request by Iraq to use its civil planes to fly the pilgrims to Saudi Arabia.
Some two million Moslems perform the haj which reaches its climax next week.
